text:
anita: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands — a couple of pricing/credits items came up and I wanted to capture answers here so we can action them. TL;DR: 1) can credits be tracked per-route/model? 2) what is our policy for ratecap exceptions (partners/enterprise/exemptions)? 3) burst/grace window behavior — when do we throttle vs allow short bursts?

liam: Short answers up front: credits are token-based and billed at the org/project level today. Console provides per-route usage *visibility* but not separate billing buckets.

sasha: Finance note: billing is against the org balance. We don't create multiple billing accounts per-route by default. Exceptions (i.e., marking a customer or partner as "exempt") require contract language & finance signoff — not automated today.

kevin: Ops/infra: ratecap exceptions are implemented as an allowlist flag in the control plane. Currently it's a manual process: support creates an exemption and Ops flips the flag. No self-serve UI yet.

anita: Do we have an SLA for processing exemption requests? Customers asked about <24h turnaround for urgent partner integrations.

kevin: For standard support tickets we'll target 48h. For enterprise customers we aim for 24h. For emergencies we can temporarily issue manual burst keys (short-lived) while the exemption is processed.

liam: Technical detail on burst behavior: we use a token-bucket rate limiter with a default burst window ~30s. Short spikes within the bucket are allowed; sustained overage results in backpressure and 429s. Dedicated/Private deployments can expose per-org rate-limit tuning.

sasha: Also clarifying "grace credits": we don't auto-grant goodwill credits. Sales/RevOps can authorize one-off credit adjustments; finance needs a standardized approval workflow. We'll provide a template.

maria: Leadership: good discussion. We're putting per-route billing granularity and a self-serve exemption UI on the roadmap. Action plan: internal RFC + engineering spike next sprint, public ETA tentatively Q3. We'll follow up with an FAQ to avoid confusion.

anita: Great — can someone file the RFC and create a doc stub that we can point customers to? I'll coordinate messaging with PMM.

deploy-bot: docs: /docs/ops/credits-exemptions.md created by liam — https://redwood.docs/credits-exemptions :tada:

anita: Thanks. Can we also include a sample policy snippet showing how to mark an org as exempt? That would help SREs and partners.

liam: Sample (short): `rate_limit_exempt: true // per-org-id` — full example will go in the docs page with config + caveats.

kevin: I'll put together an emergency runbook for issuing temporary burst tokens and for revoking them.

sasha: I'll draft the finance approval template and share in #finance-review so legal + sales can sign off.

anita: Awesome — tagging follow-ups: @liam (RFC + sample), @kevin (runbook), @sasha (finance template). I'll add this thread to the all-hands notes and ping PMM for the public FAQ.

maria: Thanks everyone — please add estimated timelines to the RFC so we can communicate expectations. :thumbsup:
